context.problem_statement: Detect distribution shift in credit scores between a training cohort (2022) and a recent scoring cohort (2024). Use the Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test to compare the distributions. Additionally compute: (1) Population Stability Index (PSI) using 10 equal-width bins, (2) mean and standard deviation shift between periods, (3) percentage of 2024 scores falling outside the 2022 distribution's 5th-99th percentile range. Flag if PSI > 0.25 (significant shift) or KS p-value < 0.05.
context.expert_knowledge: KS statistic measures maximum difference between CDFs; use scipy.stats.ks_2samp. PSI = sum((actual_pct - expected_pct) * ln(actual_pct / expected_pct)) over bins. PSI < 0.1: no shift, 0.1-0.25: moderate shift, > 0.25: significant shift requiring model retraining. Credit score drift can indicate economic changes, population shift, or data pipeline issues.
